## Overview

GitHub says workflow dependency lockfiles for GitHub Actions are now in public preview. In a changelog entry dated October 14, 2026, [GitHub states](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-14-github-actions-workflow-lockfiles-in-public-preview) that the feature is available on "GitHub Enterprise Cloud, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency, Team, and Free plans." The entry also carries an editor's note, dated the same day, saying it "Updated which plans have access to this publi...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (850 words by the writer's count; independently counted 850 raw and 850 with link URLs stripped, within the 400-1200 News range). Title is 131 characters, under the 150 cap. Clear sections: lead with plan list and editor's note, GitHub's described motivation and tooling, Dependabot and docs detail, preview caveats from the repository README, and an explicit 'What the Sources Do Not Say' section. No internal links (all three links point to the cited external sources). No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: PR checked out via refs/pull/2632/head fetch and the submission read with git show (worktree-safe); confirmed by title and path that the copy is the PR's single submission file (exactly one file changed in the PR, no stray files). Hash and ed25519 signature valid per chief:review. All three snapshots exist (status 200, gzipped) and contain the page body, not only chrome. source-0.html.gz (github.blog changelog, Oct 14 2026): confirms 'GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfiles are now in public preview for GitHub Enterprise Cloud, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency, Team, and Free plans'; editor's note '(October 14th, 2026): Updated which plans have access to this public preview.' (earlier plan list not stated, as the article says); 'gh actions-lock' extension name; '.github/workflows/actions.lock' with 'reviewable commits for actions and their transitive dependencies, as well as reusable workflow dependencies'; the four capabilities; 'The Require lockfile policy is also available in public preview' for enterprise, organization and repository administrators (no default, pricing or GA date stated); Dependabot regenerates the matching lockfile entry 'without additional configuration'; credits to Andrew Nesbitt, Francois Proulx, Jesse Houwing and William Woodruff 'over the past year'; quoted sentences ('Tags and branches can move...', 'Locking does not determine...', 'without modifying files, including in a CI check') are verbatim. source-1.html.gz (docs.github.com): confirms 'should never be edited by hand', 'must exist within a branch of the source repository', the example file with ref, commit, owner_id, repo_id and version 'v0.0.2' (docs-only details, attributed to the docs), the owner_id/repo_id run-time identity purpose, 'public preview and subject to change', and the SHA pinning passage ('no longer necessary'). source-2.html.gz (raw README of github/gh-actions-lock): confirms 'pre-1.0 and under active development', 'may change without notice between releases', 'GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) is not supported', 'best-effort and community-based' support, --verify, --verify-local ('only checks that every ref has a lockfile entry, not that the entries are trustworthy'), 'not advanced when upstream moves', --relock, 'cannot use local-path actions' / 'short-term gap'. Single-source details (GHES, pre-1.0, --verify-local/--relock from README; owner_id/repo_id and v0.0.2 from docs; plan list, Dependabot and credits from changelog) are each attributed to their source in the article. Title claims verified: 'Public Preview' (changelog), 'gh actions-lock Extension' (exact extension name in changelog, docs and README), 'Require Lockfile Policy' (changelog 'Require lockfile' policy; title-cased). Live re-fetch on Oct 15 2026: changelog (HTTP 200) still lists the same four plans and the same editor's note; docs page (HTTP 200) unchanged on the reusable-workflow exception and v0.0.2; README live bytes hash identical to the snapshot (sha256 4cdbcfa7...). No changes found. suspicious_patterns is null for all three sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Both flagged inconsistencies exist as described and are reported fairly without picking a side. (1) Docs: lockfile 'extends to transitive dependencies ... except for dependencies of reusable workflow calls. A reusable workflow is covered by the lockfile of the repository where it is defined'; changelog: lockfile includes 'reusable workflow dependencies'. The article calls this a difference in emphasis and says the pages do not explain how the statements fit; this is cautious wording (the docs also say the lockfile pins 'reusable workflow' dependencies elsewhere, so the two may be reconcilable, which the article does not assert). (2) README limitations: 'Workflows in the lockfile cannot use local-path actions' vs. the README's section saying same-repo './' composite action references are converted to '$/' on fix runs and '$/' needs no lockfile entry; the article states the README does not reconcile them. All vendor claims are attributed to GitHub; the article states no adoption figures or independent testing exist in the sources. Freshness: changelog dated Oct 14 2026, README read Oct 15 2026; the plan list was revised after the original posting, which the article discloses.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributed throughout ('GitHub states', 'Per the changelog', 'the docs say'). No sensationalism or editorializing.
